title: The Example of Good and Bad Companions
summary: The Hadith illustrates the impact of good and bad company. Good companions are likened to a musk carrier who spreads pleasant fragrance, while bad companions are compared to a blacksmith's bellows, which produce an unpleasant odor. This emphasizes the benefits of associating with righteous people and the harms of bad company.
translation: It is important to remember that the company of righteous people leads to goodness for us and our families. By being with good people, we are influenced by their virtues. This is why the Quran orders, 'O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.' Similarly, Hadiths encourage and advise us to join gatherings of good people. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) explained that someone who keeps good company is like a musk carrier, and someone with bad company is like a blacksmith’s bellows. The musk carrier either shares the fragrance with you or you might buy from him, and even if neither, you will at least experience its scent. In contrast, the blacksmith’s bellows either burn your clothes or at least give off an unpleasant smell. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'The example of a good companion and a bad companion is like the possessor of musk and the one blowing bellows. The possessor of musk will either offer you some, you will buy it, or at least enjoy a good smell from it. The one blowing bellows will either burn your clothes or you will get a foul smell.' Hence, it is explained through examples that associating with good people results in goodness, and with bad people results in harm. As the poet says, when I gain the company of Allah's people, it feels like heaven has descended to earth. Therefore, associating with righteous people brings benefits in this world and the hereafter, while bad company results in losses.
